name: stack-step-carousel
title: Stack Step Carousel
description: A full-bleed background modelling vacuum thin-film deposition on a planetary carrier: 8 mirror/lens blanks ride a slowly rotating carrier ring past a fixed 30-degree source arc, each pass stepping that blank's reflectance up a notch along a real quarter-wave-stack recursion, staggered swaps keeping the batch permanently mid-cycle.
useWhen: a full-bleed backdrop wants an 'industrial batch process quietly running behind the copy' identity built on a real, continuously-decaying-then-resetting per-unit progression (each of several discrete units steps up independently and reloads on its own staggered clock, never all together) rather than one single global progress state. Pick weld-pool instead when the identity should be a single continuous molten surface with no discrete countable units at all, or aspheric-turn-spiral when the point is one lens surface's own slow radial feed reversing (a single continuous process, not many independently-staggered units on a shared carrier).
instruction: A full-bleed single-canvas background modelling vacuum thin-film deposition on a planetary carrier. N_DISCS = 8 substrate discs sit on station points evenly spaced (45deg apart) around a single sun-ring circle of radius 0.32*min(w,h) centered on the container; disc radius = 0.09*min(w,h). The whole ring IS the carrier: station angle for disc i is i*(2*PI/8), and its live angular position is stationAngle_i + orbitAngle(t) where orbitAngle(t) = 2*PI*t/ORBIT_PERIOD_S (ORBIT_PERIOD_S = 14, the spec's 'sun ring / carrier period') with t real elapsed wall-clock seconds since mount and NO loop reset ever — the process genuinely never finishes, matching the source process running continuously rather than as a one-shot flash. layerAt(station, t) = (seedOffset_i + floor(t/14 + stationAngle_i/(2*PI))) mod 13: floor(...) is the disc's own completed-orbit count (a step function ticking up exactly once per 14s per disc, offset per station, so a NEW crossing lands somewhere on the 8-disc ring roughly every 14/8=1.75s even though any single disc's own personal orbit is 14s); mod 13 gives a 0..12 cycle where 12 (full stack) rolling to 0 on the next crossing IS the staggered fresh-blank swap the spec calls for, and because every disc shares the identical 14s cycle rate, the per-disc seedOffset_i (a fixed integer 0..12 from a seeded mulberry32(0x5ea70c1e) PRNG, never Math.random) that staggers each disc's starting phase persists as a permanent offset forever — the batch is structurally incapable of resyncing into one synchronized reload. Independent of orbital position, every disc ALSO spins on its own local axis at SPIN_PERIOD_S = 3.5 (the spec's literal 4:1 gear ratio against the 14s carrier) — a real, separate mechanism in planetary coating rigs (substrates spin on their own mount for uniform deposition) rendered as a faint --border radial tick sweeping the disc face, deliberately decoupled from the crossing/layer-step cadence per the round-9 decoupling rule rather than driven 1:1 into it. Reflectance is the real quarter-wave-stack recursion: Y(N) = n_sub*(n_L/n_H)^N, R(N) = ((n_air-Y)/(n_air+Y))^2 for a symmetric alternating H/L stack (n_air=1, n_H=2.35 TiO2-like, n_L=1.38 SiO2-like, n_sub=1.52 glass-like), giving R(0)~4% (bare glass) climbing with the real diminishing-returns shape to R(12)~99% (a realistic 12-layer HR mirror); normalized to reflectanceFrac = (R(N)-R(0))/(R(12)-R(0)) in 0..1, this is a plain linear RGB mix (parseHex'd once from the read tokens, no color-space claims beyond that) between --ns-muted (0, bare) and --foreground (1, fully stacked) — since --foreground is by definition the maximum-contrast token against --background in every theme, 'fully stacked reads as the higher-contrast extreme, never a different hue' (the weld-pool convention's intent) holds structurally with no separate bias/contrast pair needed. Each disc's source-crossing glow uses crossingAge(station,t) = time since its last top-crossing (0..14s, wrapping); while under GLOW_MS=800 a soft halo (plain --foreground alpha-only fill at 1.45x disc radius, never --ns-accent) rises linearly to a peak at GLOW_PEAK_MS=150 then fades back to 0 by 800ms — arrives, brightens, departs, never a blink; the fixed source arc itself (a 30deg --border stroke at the top of the sun ring, from -105deg to -75deg in canvas terms) brightens slightly (alpha 0.6 to 1.0) whenever any disc's glow is active, tying the two together. Pointer: a wrap-level pointermove finds the nearest disc whose center is within 1.3x its radius and sets hoverIndex; a hoverAlpha value eases toward 1 (or 0) at a fixed per-frame rate approximating a ~150ms response, and while eased-in draws a --foreground outline ring at 1.2x disc radius whose alpha is 0.3 + that disc's OWN current reflectanceFrac*0.4 (a legible 'how far along this one is' cue) — no accent tint anywhere, and hover never touches orbit or spin rate. Colour is read once via getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue for --foreground, --ns-muted (both parsed from hex to RGB, no literal fallback) and --border (used as a CSS color string directly) with no literal fallback of any kind; if any is empty the mount loop retries on the next rAF and paints nothing until all three resolve. A MutationObserver on document.documentElement's class attribute re-reads tokens on every theme flip and forces a resize+redraw; a ResizeObserver on the wrapper recomputes geometry (station positions and disc radius both derive from the container's own min(w,h)) and resizes the canvas backing store (capped devicePixelRatio 2); an IntersectionObserver stops driving new frames while off-screen and, on re-entering view, re-reads tokens and resumes — because position is derived from absolute elapsed wall time rather than accumulated per-frame deltas, the carrier is exactly where continuous real-time rotation would have put it, never a stale resume. autoplay is 'none' because the carrier turns on its own internal wall-clock regardless of pointer/scroll/press input — there is nothing for the site's synthetic-input driver to do, and the pointer halo is a hover-only affordance, not something a scripted input pass should trigger. Under prefers-reduced-motion the component runs zero rAF loops and zero timers: it draws exactly one static frame at t = GLOW_PEAK_MS/1000 = 0.15s, at which station 0 (angle 0, i.e. starting exactly at the top) sits at its glow's precise peak (a bright halo on one disc, mid-crossing under the source, named 'carrier-crossing') while the other 7 stations sit at their own staggered natural positions and pre-crossing layer counts from seedOffset_i alone — the same deterministic frame every load; a resize under reduced motion redraws that same frozen instant rather than advancing it. Cleanup on unmount cancels both the animation and token-wait rAF handles, disconnects all three observers, and removes both pointer listeners. Zero dependencies, DOM+canvas only, no color literal anywhere including fallbacks, no hue anywhere (monochrome value-only ramp).
